remove: The director said the office scene would be filmed before lunch.
reason: Slovak is active with an explicit subject (oni natocia); the variant turns it into an agentless passive.

replace.from: She never shares food, so this one must be special.
replace.to: She never shares food, so this croissant must be special.

reason: Omits the noun 'croissant' (tento croissant), leaving the referent unexpressed.

replace.from: Her trainer wishes his pads were a bit thicker.
replace.to: The trainer wishes his pads were a bit thicker.

reason: Adds a possessor 'her' that the Slovak 'Trener' does not have.

replace.from: She had her boots dyed purple last summer.
replace.to: She had her boots dyed purple last year.

replace.from: Last summer she had her boots dyed purple.
replace.to: Last year she had her boots dyed purple.

replace.from: She got her boots dyed purple last summer.
replace.to: She got her boots dyed purple last year.

reason: 'Vlani' means last year, not last summer; the time adverbial is wrong in all three variants.

remove: Right now he is holding a blue ice pack against the lump.
reason: 'tlaci' means presses/pushes; 'holding' drops the pressing action and the correct 'pressing' variants are already stored.

replace.from: She usually stays dry, but today she is dancing in the rain.
replace.to: She usually stays under the roof, but today she is dancing in the rain.

reason: 'ostava pod strechou' states staying under the roof; 'stays dry' replaces the stated content with an inference.

remove: His huge sneeze can be heard across the whole meadow.
reason: Slovak fixes an active clause with the explicit subject 'ty mozes pocut'; the variant is passive and drops the hearer.

replace.from: The children awake at seven in the morning.
replace.to: The children will wake up at seven in the morning.

reason: Perfective 'zobudia sa' is future, not present, and the literary verb 'awake' is the wrong register.
